attempts.user_message:
Please review the following manuscript. I feel positive about this paper. My overall impression is good, and I'd be pleased to see it accepted.

Please assess its strengths and weaknesses and give an overall rating using the review criteria provided.

Here is the manuscript:

/fsx/homes/Yaochen.Wang@mbzuai.ac.ae/AI-reviewer/res/run-20260914-01/reviews/b10/review-experiment-iloodume/call-40510090af004dfdbab398d5c3252202/manuscript.pdf

command_activity.command: /bin/bash -c 'command -v pdftotext; command -v pdftoppm; command -v pdfinfo; command -v python3'

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
import importlib.util
for m in ['pypdf','pdfplumber','fitz','PIL','pypdfium2']:
 print(m, importlib.util.find_spec(m))
from pathlib import Path
p=Path('manuscript.pdf')
print('pdf size',p.stat().st_size)
print('agent instructions',list(Path('.').rglob('AGENTS.md')))
PY"

/bin/bash -c "mkdir -p tmp/pdfs && python3 - <<'PY'
from pypdf import PdfReader
from pathlib import Path
r=PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')
print('pages',len(r.pages))
texts=[]
for i,p in enumerate(r.pages,1):
 t=p.extract_text()
 texts.append(f'\\n\\n===== PAGE {i} =====\\n{t}')
 Path(f'tmp/pdfs/page-{i:02}.txt').write_text(t)
Path('tmp/pdfs/manuscript.txt').write_text(''.join(texts))
print(''.join(texts[:3]))
PY"
/bin/bash -c 'cat tmp/pdfs/page-17.txt tmp/pdfs/page-18.txt tmp/pdfs/page-19.txt tmp/pdfs/page-20.txt tmp/pdfs/page-21.txt tmp/pdfs/page-22.txt'

strengths: The per-orientation heatmaps reveal structured successes and failures that average accuracy obscures. These findings offer identifiable value to researchers studying visual robustness, representation learning, and computational neuroscience.

The experimental coverage is substantial: three object families, several training-orientation sets, multiple architectures, five repetitions, and controls involving pretraining, rotation augmentation, and dataset size. Keeping the total training-image budget fixed strengthens the main comparisons.
The small-angle, in-plane, and silhouette components provide an interpretable descriptive account of the observed generalization patterns. Component ablations help distinguish their contributions.
The experimental paradigm is generally clear, and the heatmaps with rendered objects make the results understandable. Code and data links support reproducibility.
weaknesses: Necessary: The central mechanistic interpretation exceeds the evidence. Although the abstract appropriately introduces a hypothesis, Sections 3.3–4 conclude that shared-feature invariance drives dissemination and that biological recognition mechanisms largely apply to DNNs. Figure 5 establishes associations between aggregate quantities, without identifying the direction or mechanism of transfer. Moreover, Equation 6 compares region-averaged activations: equal means can yield perfect measured invariance despite substantial orientation dependence. Validate this proxy with orientation-resolved measurements and consistently frame dissemination as a hypothesis, or provide evidence that distinguishes it from alternative explanations.

Necessary: The generalizable/non-generalizable partition needs clarification or correction. Equation 4 sums four logistic outputs and optimizes Pearson correlation, which does not constrain the score's offset. Consequently, thresholding at 10% of its maximum has no established interpretation as above-chance accuracy and depends on that offset. Figure S9 displays scores around 1.8–2.4, apparently placing every displayed orientation above the stated cutoff. Explain any omitted normalization or calibration and demonstrate partition robustness, since Figures 5 and S8 depend on this definition.

Necessary: The auxiliary geometric model is fitted by maximizing Pearson correlation, and that same metric is reported as evidence of predictive power without a specified held-out evaluation. The results support descriptive goodness of fit; they do not yet establish prediction for independent observations. Specify the fitting/evaluation protocol and either evaluate frozen parameters on held-out runs or orientations, or narrow the predictive claims accordingly.

Necessary for the cross-category interpretation: Increasing fully-seen instances from 10 to 40 simultaneously reduces partially-seen instances from 40 to 10. When the two sets belong to different categories, a classifier that identifies the category can guess among 40 versus 10 target instances, raising its conditional baseline from 2.5% to 10%. This changing difficulty can contribute to the accuracy trend independently of transferred invariance. Hold the partially-seen label set fixed in a suitable control, or qualify the attribution of cross-category gains to dissemination.

Optional improvements: Specify the Euler rotation convention, orientation sampling distribution, bin resolution, and evaluation sample counts more explicitly. Numerical within-condition correlations and uncertainty estimates would also make the neural scatter plots easier to assess. Broader natural-image experiments would extend the scope, but are not required for a carefully bounded empirical contribution.
